questions.question: Flute instruments comes under which type of instrument category?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Flute instruments** generally fall under the category of **"Sushira Vadya."**
 
• **"Sushira Vadya"** refers to **wind instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by blowing air through a hollow tube.**
 
• **The flute,** also known as "Venu" in** Indian classical music,** is a popular example of a **Sushira Vadya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghana Vadya:**

 
 
• Ghana Vadya refers to percussion instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by striking or shaking.
 
• Examples of Ghana Vadya include instruments like the mridangam and ghatam.
 
 
 
• **Sushira Vadya:**
 
 
• Sushira Vadya refers to wind instruments in Indian classical music that produce sound by blowing air into them.
 
• Flute instruments, such as the** Bansuri (a bamboo flute) or Venu, fall under this category. **
 
 
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya:**
 
 
• Avanaddha Vadya is percussion instrument. Sound is produced by a stretched membrane, such as a drum. Membranophonic instruments act as skin-vibrators because they produce sound-waves by vibrations of a stretched skin or membrane when struck, plucked, or stroked.
 
• Examples of Avanaddha Vadya include instruments like the** **Tabla, Ankya, Alingya, Oordhwaka, and Damru.

questions.question: Mame Khan, an Indian folk singer known for his Sufi and folk music performances, is from the state of _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mame Khan is a renowned Indian folk singer known for his mesmerizing Sufi and folk music performances.
 
• He hails from the state of **Rajasthan**, which is known for its rich tradition of folk music.
 
• Khan belongs to the Manganiyar community, a traditional musician caste from Rajasthan.
 
• He has performed at various national and international platforms, bringing Rajasthani folk music to a global audience.
 
• Khan's music often features traditional instruments like the khartal, dholak, and harmonium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rajasthani Folk Music**

 
 
• Rajasthani folk music is characterized by its distinct melodies and rhythms, often reflecting the region's history and culture.
 
• It includes various forms such as Maand, Bhopa-Bhopi, and Panihari, each with its unique style and significance.
 
• Instruments commonly used include the sarangi, kamayacha, and morchang.
 
• This musical tradition is often passed down orally through generations within specific communities.
 
 
 
• **Manganiyar Community**
 
 
• The Manganiyars are a community of hereditary musicians in Rajasthan and parts of Sindh in Pakistan.
 
• They traditionally serve as court musicians for Rajput patrons but also perform for various social and religious events.
 
• Their music often includes themes of devotion, love, and historical tales.
 
• The community has been instrumental in keeping the folk music traditions alive and vibrant.
 
 
 
• **Sufi Music**
 
 
• Sufi music is a genre of music inspired by Sufism, the mystical dimension of Islam.
 
• It aims to induce a state of spiritual trance and is often performed during Sufi gatherings and festivals.
 
• Instruments like the tabla, harmonium, and sitar are commonly used in Sufi music.
 
• Prominent forms include Qawwali and Ghazal, which have found a significant place in South Asian music culture.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition**
 
 
• Rajasthani folk music, including the performances by artists like Mame Khan, has gained international acclaim.
 
• These artists have performed at prestigious festivals and events around the world, promoting cultural exchange.
 
• Efforts by the government and cultural organizations have helped in preserving and promoting this rich heritage.
 
• Documentaries and music albums featuring Rajasthani folk music have contributed to its global popularity.

questions.question: Theyyam dance, performed to appease and make peace with the Gods who ensure good harvest and prosperity, is popular in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Theyyam** is a traditional dance form that is highly popular in the state of Kerala.
 
• It is performed to appease and make peace with the Gods who are believed to ensure good harvest and prosperity.
 
• Theyyam is also known as **Kaliyattam** and is characterized by elaborate costumes, vibrant makeup, and intense dance movements.
 
• This dance form is rooted in the **ritualistic traditions** of Kerala and is performed in temples and sacred groves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Theyyam**

 
 
• Theyyam is a popular Hindu ritual form of worship in Kerala, India.
 
• It encompasses dance, mime, and music, and enshrines the rudiments of ancient tribal cultures, which attached great importance to the worship of heroes and the spirits of ancestors.
 
• The performers of Theyyam belong to the lower caste community, and through the performance, they are elevated to a divine status.
 
• Theyyam is performed from December to April, and over 400 different forms of Theyyam exist today.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Makeup**
 
 
• The costumes and makeup of Theyyam are elaborate and vibrant, with significant use of face paints, masks, and headgear.
 
• The makeup is often done by the performers themselves, and it can take several hours to complete.
 
• The costumes include coconut leaves, cloth, and other natural materials, and they play a crucial role in defining the character being portrayed.
 
 
 
• **Ritualistic Significance**
 
 
• Theyyam is deeply intertwined with the spiritual and religious life of the people in Kerala.
 
• The performance is believed to bring blessings, protection, and prosperity to the community.
 
• It is also a means of storytelling, where myths and legends are narrated through the dance and music.
 
 
 
• **Modern Influence**
 
 
• Theyyam has gained popularity beyond Kerala and is now performed at cultural festivals and events across India and the world.
 
• Despite its traditional roots, Theyyam has adapted to contemporary times while retaining its core essence.

• Khayal is a form of Hindustani classical music that emphasizes improvisation and emotional expression.
 
• It is characterized by its two main sections: the slow tempo "Vilambit" and the fast tempo "Drut."
 
• Khayal singing often incorporates intricate ornamentation and raga exploration.

• Lalit Kala Kendra, established by Bhimsen Joshi, is a prestigious institute for performing arts education in Pune.
 
• It offers specialized training in various traditional Indian art forms, including classical music, dance, and drama.
 
• The center aims to preserve and promote India's rich cultural heritage.

• Bhimsen Joshi received the Bharat Ratna in 2008 for his unparalleled contributions to Indian music.

• Bhimsen Joshi belonged to the **Kirana Gharana**, known for its emphasis on melody and emotional depth.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is normally played in a vertical position and with an arched bow?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Sarangi**

__
 
• It is also called **saran **or **Saranga**, short-necked fiddle used throughout South Asia, particularly for folk and classical Hindustani music. Measuring about 76 cm (30 inches) long, the instrument has a roughly rectangular slightly waisted body and broad fretless neck generally carved from a single piece of wood.
 
• It has three melody strings made of gut, usually tuned a fifth and a fourth apart, and 11 to 37 sympathetically vibrating metal strings.
 
• **The musician, who is seated, normally holds the instrument against his left shoulder in a vertical position and plays with an arched bow held in an underhand grip in his right hand. Hence, Option 4 is correct.**
 
• The cuticles (or sometimes the space on the fingernail just above the cuticles) of the left hand are pressed against the strings to sound specific pitches.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a96a6d6b9106400bfc249da27121877dc089d6af73e6eb6d9a6708ee955316c7.png] ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Shehnai**

 
• **It is double-reed conical oboe of North India**.
 
• The Shehnai is made of wood, except for a flaring metal bell attached to the bottom of the instrument, and measures about 12–20 inches (30–50 cm) in length, with six to eight keyless finger holes along its body.

**Veena**

 
• **It is among the oldest Indian musical instruments.**
 
• From the references to Vedic writings, it can date back to around the first millennium B.C. Temple sculptures from the 2nd century B.C. show a type of veena being played.
 
• The Saraswati Veena is predominant in Carnatic music and the Rudra veena is the most played veena in Hindustani music.
 
• The Saraswati veena has seven strings strung over twenty-four fixed frets.
 
• It is played by sitting cross-legged, with the resonator to the player's right.
 
• The veena is said to be the** only instrument that can play all the Gamakas **(oscillations) in Carnatic music, usually something that only the most proficient vocalists can achieve.
 
• The Hindu Goddess of Knowledge, Saraswati, is said to play the Veena.
 
• Pictures depict her sitting on a lotus and playing the instrument.

**Sitar**

 
• **It is a **stringed instrument of the lute family that is popular in northern **India, Pakistan, **and **Bangladesh**.
 
• The instrument was invented in medieval India, flourished in the 16th and 17th centuries, and arrived at its present form in 18th-century India.
 
• Used widely throughout the Indian subcontinent, the sitar became popularly known in the wider world through the works of **Ravi Shankar**, beginning in the late 1950s and early 1960s.

questions.question: Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. It is celebrated in which of the following states?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba is a unique festival celebrating the onset of the monsoon and the earth’s womanhood. **

 
 
• **It is celebrated in Odisha**.
 
• The second day of the festival signifies the beginning of the solar month of Mithuna, during which the season of rains starts.
 
• It falls in mid-June, the first day is called Pahili Raja, the second day is Mithuna Sankranti, the third day is Bhudaaha or Basi Raja.
 
• The final fourth day is called Basumati snana, in which the ladies bathe the grinding stone as a symbol of Bhumi with turmeric paste and adore with flower, sindoor, etc.
 
• All types of seasonal fruits are offered to** mother Bhumi**.
 
• The day before the first day is called Sajabaja or preparatory day during which the house, kitchen including grinding stones are cleaned, spices are ground for three days.
 
• During these three days, women and girls take a rest from work and wear new Saree, Alata, and ornaments.
 
• It is similar to **Ambubachi Mela**.
 
• It is believed that the mother Goddess Earth or the divine wife of Lord Vishnu undergoes menstruation during the first three days.
 
• The fourth day is called Vasumati Snana, or the ceremonial bath of Bhudevi.
 
• The term Raja came from the Sanskrit word 'Rajas' which means menstruation and when a woman menstruates, she is called 'Rajaswala' or a menstruating woman, and in medieval times the festival became more popular as an agricultural holiday marking the worship of Bhudevi, who is the wife of Lord Jagannath.
 
• A silver idol of **Bhudevi **is still to be found in the Puri Temple beside Lord Jagannath.

questions.question: The Tolkappiyam is

options.text: A Tamil poem in praise of Rajendra Chola.
An ancient didactic work in Tamil.
A drama composed by a Chera King.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Tolkappiyam:**

__
 
• **The Sangam literature includes Tolkappiyam**, Ettutogai, Pattuppattu, Pathinenkilkanakku, and two epics named – Silappathikaram and Manimegalai .
 
• **Tolkappiyam was authored by Tolkappiyar** and is considered the **earliest of Tamil literary works.**
 
• Though it is a work on Tamil grammar, **it also provides insights into the political and socio-economic conditions of the time.**
 
• It is a **unique work on grammar and poetics**, in its three parts of nine sections each, deals with Ezhuttu(letter), Col (word) and Porul (subject matter).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Almost all levels of the human language from the spoken to the most poetic lie within the purview of Tolkappiyar’s analysis as he treats exquisitely** poetic and epigrammatic statements on phonology, morphology, syntax, rhetoric, prosody and poetics.**
 
• According to the traditional legend, **the original grammar was called Agathiam written down by sage Agastya, but it went missing after a great deluge.**
 
• Tolkappiyam refers to the Five-fold division of lands – **Kurinji (hilly tracks), Mullai (pastoral), Marudam (agricultural), Neydal (coastal) and Palai (desert).**
 
• Tolkappiyam also refers to four castes namely **arasar(Ruling Class), anthanar, vanigar(carried on trade and commerce) and vellalar(Agriculturists).**
 
• Ancient primitive tribes like **Thodas, Irulas, Nagas and Vedars lived in this period.**
